# Introduction
Example 2 of the paper "Confidence intervals for the F1-score in medical object
detection: comparing bootstrap and Bayesian multilevel methods".

Code and data: <https://github.com/ndevln/f1-score-ci-object-detection> (data: `S2_Data_MIDOG_Models.csv`).

This script estimates the F1-score and its 95% confidence/
credible interval on the MIDOG 2022 Challenge dataset 
(Aubreville et al. 2024, <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.media.2022.102699>):
3 baseline ML models evaluated on 100 images spanning 10 domains (0-213 mitotic
figures per image).

Two methods, each for two estimands:

- Methods: bootstrap and Bayesian multilevel model (binomial + Poisson).
- Estimands: pooled (sum TP/FP/FN over the images, then compute the metric) and
  grouped (compute the metric per image, then average it).

The script has two parts:

- Part A - overall F1-score CI per model, both methods and both estimands.
- Part B - per-domain F1-score CI to probe domain generalization: bootstrap within
  each domain, and the Bayesian model with Domain as a fixed effect.

All intervals are 95% quantile intervals (QI, percentile interval), the point
estimate is the median of the bootstrap or posterior draws. Images without objects
(Case A, 4 of 100 images) are excluded and evaluated separately.

# Setup
## Load Packages
```{r}
# Seed (Article Number of the MIDOG Paper)
set.seed(102699)

# Data manipulation and visualisation
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggdist)

# Bayesian packages
library(brms)       # Fits the multilevel models via Stan
library(tidybayes)  # median_qi()/epred_draws() helpers for posterior summaries
```

## Functions
The F1-score is computed from the counts (paper eq. 3):
$$F_1 = \frac{2\,TP}{P + TP + FP}, \qquad P = TP + FN$$
Unlike the F1-score from the harmonic mean of precision and recall this formula is defined if TP = 0.

`format_result()` prints a point estimate with its interval as "0.65 (0.62 - 0.69)".
```{r}
calc_F1_score <- function(TP, FP, P) {
  2 * TP / (P + TP + FP)
}

format_result <- function(value, .lower, .upper) {
  fmt <- scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01, trim = F)
  glue::glue("{fmt(value)} ({fmt(.lower)} - {fmt(.upper)})")
}
```


## Load Data
```{r}
# One row per (model, slide): per-image confusion-matrix counts (TP/FP/FN) for each
# of the 3 baseline models, plus the Domain label (10 tissue/tumor types).
df_models <- readr::read_csv("S2_Data_MIDOG_Models.csv")
```

## Prepare Data

```{r}
df_models |>
  mutate(
    Domain = as.factor(Domain),   # treat the 10 domains as a categorical grouping
    GroundTruth = TP + FN,    # Sensitivity/recall trials: all true objects (Positives P)
    # Per-image point metrics
    Precision = pmax(0, (TP/(TP + FP)), na.rm = T), # Set to 0 if TP + FP = 0
    Recall = (TP/(TP + FN)),  # Cave: Not defined for images without true objects (P = 0)
    F1 = calc_F1_score(TP, FP, GroundTruth)
  ) |>
  # Exclude images without objects: F1-score is undefined
  filter(GroundTruth > 0) -> df_models_prep
```

# Negative Controls
Images without objects (P = 0) do not contribute to the F1-score (no TP or FN) and are reported
separately.
```{r}
df_models |>
  filter(TP + FN == 0) |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    `n images`          = n(),
    `n correct (no FP)` = sum(FP == 0),
    `FP total`          = sum(FP),
    `FP per image`      = paste(FP, collapse = ", ")
  )
```

# Objects per Domain
Images with objects per domain (the ground truth is the same for all models): objects per image
P (median and range), images with at most 5 objects, objects in total, and the share of all
images and objects. Images with few
objects make up a relevant share of the images, but only a small share of the objects, so they
contribute little to the pooled estimand (all objects weighted equally) and fully to the grouped
estimand (all images weighted equally).
```{r}
df_models_prep |>
  filter(model == "Model 1") |>
  mutate(Domain = as.character(Domain)) -> df_objects

# Domains and a total row
bind_rows(df_objects, mutate(df_objects, Domain = "Total")) |>
  mutate(Domain = factor(Domain, levels = c(1:10, "Total"))) |>
  group_by(Domain) |>
  summarise(
    Images = n(),
    `P median (range)` = sprintf("%g (%d-%d)", median(GroundTruth),
                                 min(GroundTruth), max(GroundTruth)),
    `P <= 5` = sum(GroundTruth <= 5),
    Objects = sum(GroundTruth)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    `% images`  = round(100 * Images / nrow(df_objects), 1),
    `% objects` = round(100 * Objects / sum(df_objects$GroundTruth), 1)
  )
```

# Part A: Overall analysis per model
## Bootstrap

The images are resampled with replacement (K = 10,000 resamples, >= 10,000
recommended for a stable 95% CI). Both estimands are computed from the same
resampled images:

- Pooled: sum TP, FP and FN over all resampled images first, then compute the
  metrics. Images are weighted by their object count (P), so high-count images
  dominate.
- Grouped: average the per-image metrics, so every image carries equal weight
  regardless of its object count (see paper "Grouped averaging").

```{r}
K = 10000

df_models_prep |>
  select(model, TP:FN, Precision:F1) |>
  # One bootstrap "study" per .draw
  cross_join(tibble(.draw = 1:K)) |>
  group_by(model, .draw) |>
  # Resample images with replacement up to the number of observations
  slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    # POOLED
    Precision_pooled = pmax(0, sum(TP) / sum(TP + FP), na.rm = T), # 0 if TP + FP = 0
    Recall_pooled = sum(TP) / sum(TP + FN),
    F1_pooled = calc_F1_score(sum(TP), sum(FP), sum(TP + FN)),
    # GROUPED
    Precision_grouped = mean(Precision),
    Recall_grouped = mean(Recall),
    F1_grouped = mean(F1)
  ) |>
  # Long format: one row per (draw, metric, averaging)
  pivot_longer(matches("_(pooled|grouped)$"), names_to = c("name", "averaging"),
               names_sep = "_") |>
  mutate(method = "Bootstrap") -> draws_models_boot

draws_models_boot |>
  group_by(method, model, averaging, name) |>
  median_qi(value) |>
  arrange(model, name) |>
  mutate(format = format_result(value, .lower, .upper)) |>
  select(method, model, averaging, name, format)
```

## Bayesian estimation

### Fit Model
```{r}
# Split the data into one dataset per model
data_list <- df_models_prep |>
  split(~ model)

# Binomial + Poisson model
# Sensitivity Model (Recall): TP successes out of GroundTruth (= TP + FN) trials
bf_tp <- bf(TP | trials(GroundTruth) ~ 1 + (1|Slide), family = binomial())
# False positive model: FP count per image, log link
bf_fp <- bf(FP ~ 1 + (1|Slide), family = poisson())
# (1|Slide): per-image random effect in each sub-model. 
# Precision follows from both parts: recall * P / (recall * P + FP).

# Fit the model for every dataset (model) at once; default brms weakly-informative
# priors; 4 chains, 2000 warmup of 10,000 iterations.
F1_model_multi <- brm_multiple(
  formula = bf_tp + bf_fp,
  data = data_list,
  chains = 4,
  warmup = 2000,
  iter = 10000,
  seed = 102699,
  refresh = 0, # No sampling progress in the output for PDF
  combine = FALSE # Keep model results seperate
)
```

### Get Posterior Draws

The marginal estimates refer to the population of images that the observed images
represent (CAVE: if images are a convenience sample). For every posterior draw:

1. Expected TP and FP of every observed image with its fitted image effect
   (`epred_images()`, trials = 1 gives the recall, expected TP = recall $\times$ P).
2. Bayesian bootstrap weights over the images, Dirichlet(1, ..., 1) via `rexp()`, new for every draw.
3. Pooled and grouped metrics with these weights (`calc_marginal_metrics()`).

Expected counts are never 0/0, so there are no continuity problems.

```{r}
epred_images <- function(brms_model, newdata) {
  epred_draws(brms_model, newdata = newdata |> mutate(GroundTruth = 1)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(.draw, any_of("Domain"), Slide, P, .category, .epred) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = .category, values_from = .epred) |>
    mutate(
      Recall = TP,               # recall of the image
      TP = Recall * P,           # expected TP of the image
      Precision = TP / (TP + FP) # expected TP / (expected TP + expected FP)
    ) |>
    # Bayesian bootstrap weights, new for every draw
    group_by(.draw) |>
    mutate(weight = rexp(n())) |>
    ungroup()
}

calc_marginal_metrics <- function(df_images) {
  df_images |>
    summarise(
      # POOLED
      Precision_pooled = sum(weight * TP) / sum(weight * (TP + FP)),
      Recall_pooled = sum(weight * TP) / sum(weight * P),
      F1_pooled = calc_F1_score(sum(weight * TP), sum(weight * FP), sum(weight * P)),
      # GROUPED
      Precision_grouped = weighted.mean(Precision, weight),
      Recall_grouped = weighted.mean(Recall, weight),
      F1_grouped = weighted.mean(calc_F1_score(TP, FP, P), weight),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    # Long format: one row per (draw, metric, averaging)
    pivot_longer(matches("_(pooled|grouped)$"), names_to = c("name", "averaging"),
                 names_sep = "_")
}

# Per ML model: the observed images with their object count P
draws_models_bayesian <- purrr::map2_dfr(F1_model_multi, data_list, \(x, y)
  epred_images(x, newdata = y |> distinct(Slide, P = GroundTruth)) |>
    group_by(.draw) |>
    calc_marginal_metrics() |>
    mutate(model = unique(y$model))
) |>
  mutate(method = "Bayesian")
```

Point estimate (posterior median) and 95% QI per model, estimand and metric:

```{r}
draws_models_bayesian |>
  group_by(method, model, averaging, name) |>
  median_qi(value) |>
  arrange(model, name) |>
  mutate(format = format_result(value, .lower, .upper)) |>
  select(method, model, averaging, name, format)
```

## Visualization
### Figure 2
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 2: F1-score distributions of both methods and both estimands per model."
#| fig-height: 5.5
bind_rows(draws_models_boot, draws_models_bayesian) |>
  filter(name == "F1") |>
  ggplot(aes(y = interaction(method, averaging), x = value)) +
  # One distribution per method and estimand, with median point + 95% QI.
  stat_sample_slabinterval(aes(fill = method), show.legend = F,
                           point_interval = "median_qi", .width = 0.95,
                           slab_alpha = 0.7, normalize = "xy") +
  # Observed per-image F1 as points below; point size = number of objects (GroundTruth)
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(data = df_models_prep |> arrange(desc(GroundTruth)),
                            aes(x = F1, y = 0.8, size = GroundTruth),
                            alpha = 0.7, cex = 4, side = -1L, method = "compactswarm") +
  facet_grid(model ~ .) +   # one panel per ML model
  ggokabeito::scale_fill_okabe_ito() +   # colour-blind-safe palette
  ggsurveillance::scale_y_discrete_reverse(guide = legendry::guide_axis_nested(), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "F1-score", breaks = (0:10) / 10) +
  scale_size(name = "Slides (number of objects on each slide)", range = c(0.2, 2),
             breaks = c(1, 50, 100, 150)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggsurveillance::theme_mod_legend_top() +
  ggsurveillance::theme_mod_remove_minor_grid_x()
ggsave("Figure_2.pdf", width = 8, height = 5.5)
```

# Part B: Stratified analysis by Domain
Domain generalization diagnostic. The MIDOG challenge cares whether a model
performs consistently across the 10 domains. Both methods and both estimands are
computed per domain: the bootstrap resamples the images within each domain, the
Bayesian model has Domain as a fixed effect and the Bayesian bootstrap weights act
within each domain.

## Bootstrap per domain
```{r}
df_models_prep |>
  select(model, Domain, TP:FN, Precision:F1) |>
  cross_join(tibble(.draw = 1:K)) |>
  # Stratify by Domain: resampling happens within each domain
  group_by(model, Domain, .draw) |>
  # Resample with replacement up to the number of observations
  slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    # POOLED
    Precision_pooled = pmax(0, sum(TP) / sum(TP + FP), na.rm = T), # 0 if TP + FP = 0
    Recall_pooled = sum(TP) / sum(TP + FN),
    F1_pooled = calc_F1_score(sum(TP), sum(FP), sum(TP + FN)),
    # GROUPED
    Precision_grouped = mean(Precision),
    Recall_grouped = mean(Recall),
    F1_grouped = mean(F1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # Long format: one row per (domain, draw, metric, averaging)
  pivot_longer(matches("_(pooled|grouped)$"), names_to = c("name", "averaging"),
               names_sep = "_") |>
  mutate(method = "Bootstrap\n(stratified)") -> draws_models_boot_domain
```

## Bayesian model with domain as fixed effect
```{r}
# Re-split per model (as before) and refit with Domain added as a fixed effect
# This is the Bayesian analogue of the domain-stratified bootstrap.
data_list <- df_models_prep |>
  split(~ model)

# Binomial + Poisson model as above, with Domain as fixed effect
# Sensitivity Model (Recall): Domain fixed effect + per-image random effect
bf_tp_d <- bf(TP | trials(GroundTruth) ~ Domain + (1|Slide), family = binomial())
# False positive model: same structure
bf_fp_d <- bf(FP ~ Domain + (1|Slide), family = poisson())

# Fit per model; same sampler settings as the non-stratified model above.
F1_model_domain_multi <- brm_multiple(
  formula = bf_tp_d + bf_fp_d,
  data = data_list,
  chains = 4,
  warmup = 2000,
  iter = 10000,
  seed = 102699,
  refresh = 0,
  combine = FALSE
)
```

Marginal estimates per domain as in Part A, with `epred_images()` and
`calc_marginal_metrics()` per domain and posterior draw.

```{r}
draws_models_bayesian_domain <- purrr::map2_dfr(F1_model_domain_multi, data_list, \(x, y)
  epred_images(x, newdata = y |> distinct(Domain, Slide, P = GroundTruth)) |>
    group_by(Domain, .draw) |>
    calc_marginal_metrics() |>
    mutate(model = unique(y$model))
) |>
  mutate(method = "Bayesian\n(fixed effect)")
```

## Visualization
### Figure 3
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 3: F1-score distributions per domain, both methods, pooled estimand."
#| fig-height: 5
bind_rows(draws_models_boot_domain, draws_models_bayesian_domain) |>
  filter(name == "F1") -> draws_models_domain_F1

draws_models_domain_F1 |>
  filter(averaging == "pooled") |>
  ggplot(aes(y = method, x = value)) +
  # One coloured density slab per domain (adjust = 3 smooths the discrete bootstrap).
  stat_slab(aes(fill = Domain), show.legend = F, slab_alpha = 0.6, normalize = "xy",
            adjust = 3, linewidth = 0.2, color = "black") +
  # Observed per-image F1 below, grouped on the y-axis by domain (1 - Domain/10) and
  # coloured by domain; point size = number of objects on the slide.
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(data = df_models_prep |> arrange(desc(GroundTruth)),
                            aes(x = F1, y = 1 - as.numeric(Domain) / 10,
                                size = GroundTruth, color = Domain),
                            alpha = 0.7, cex = 2, side = -1L, dodge.width = 0.1,
                            method = "compactswarm") +
  facet_grid(model ~ .) +   # one row of panels per ML model
  ggsci::scale_fill_d3(guide = NULL) +    # 10-colour categorical palette for domains
  ggsci::scale_color_d3(guide = NULL) +
  ggsurveillance::scale_y_discrete_reverse(name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "F1-score", breaks = (0:10) / 10) +
  scale_size(name = "Slides (number of objects on each slide)", range = c(0.2, 2),
             breaks = c(1, 50, 100, 150)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggsurveillance::theme_mod_legend_top() +
  ggsurveillance::theme_mod_remove_minor_grid_x() -> fig_domain

fig_domain
ggsave("Figure_3.pdf", width = 7, height = 6)
```

### Supplement Figure S2.1
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Supplement Figure S2.1: F1-score distributions per domain, both methods, grouped estimand."
#| fig-height: 5
# Figure 3 with its data replaced by the grouped draws
fig_domain + filter(draws_models_domain_F1, averaging == "grouped")
```

# Checks
## Checks Part A
### Convergence diagnostics
```{r}
# Convergence of the fits of Part A, per ML model, over all parameters
purrr::map2_dfr(F1_model_multi, names(data_list), \(x, y) {
  df_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_array(x), "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  tibble(
    model        = y,
    max_rhat     = max(df_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ess_bulk = min(df_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ess_tail = min(df_summary$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    divergences  = sum(subset(nuts_params(x), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
  )
})
```

```{r}
# Part A per population-level parameter (intercepts and SD of the per-image effects)
purrr::map2_dfr(F1_model_multi, names(data_list), \(x, y)
  posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_array(x, variable = "^(b|sd)_", regex = TRUE),
                             "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail") |>
    mutate(model = y, .before = 1)
)
```

### Posterior predictive check
```{r}
# TP: observed TP per image (dot) with the 50% / 90% predictive interval
purrr::map2(F1_model_multi, names(data_list), \(x, y)
  pp_check(x, resp = "TP", type = "intervals", ndraws = 1000) + ggtitle(y, "TP per image")
)
```

```{r}
# FP: rootogram of the FP counts (observed bars vs. expected frequencies)
purrr::map2(F1_model_multi, names(data_list), \(x, y)
  pp_check(x, resp = "FP", type = "rootogram", ndraws = 1000) + ggtitle(y, "FP counts")
)
```

```{r}
# TP per image, predicted as new images
purrr::map2(F1_model_multi, data_list, \(x, y)
  pp_check(x, resp = "TP", type = "intervals", ndraws = 1000,
           newdata = y |> mutate(Slide = paste0("new_", Slide)),
           allow_new_levels = TRUE, sample_new_levels = "gaussian") +
    ggtitle(unique(y$model), "TP per image, predicted as new images")
)
```

```{r}
# FP counts, predicted as new images
purrr::map2(F1_model_multi, data_list, \(x, y)
  pp_check(x, resp = "FP", type = "rootogram", ndraws = 1000,
           newdata = y |> mutate(Slide = paste0("new_", Slide)),
           allow_new_levels = TRUE, sample_new_levels = "gaussian") +
    ggtitle(unique(y$model), "FP counts, predicted as new images")
)
```

## Checks Part B
### Convergence diagnostics
```{r}
# Convergence of the fits of Part B (Domain as fixed effect), same diagnostics
purrr::map2_dfr(F1_model_domain_multi, names(data_list), \(x, y) {
  df_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_array(x), "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  tibble(
    model        = y,
    max_rhat     = max(df_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ess_bulk = min(df_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ess_tail = min(df_summary$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    divergences  = sum(subset(nuts_params(x), Parameter == "divergent__")$Value)
  )
})
```

### Posterior predictive check
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
# TP: observed TP per image (dot) with the 50% / 90% predictive interval, per domain
purrr::map2(F1_model_domain_multi, names(data_list), \(x, y)
  pp_check(x, resp = "TP", type = "intervals_grouped", group = "Domain", ndraws = 1000) +
    ggtitle(y, "TP per image, by domain")
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
# FP: rootogram of the FP counts (observed bars vs. expected frequencies)
purrr::map2(F1_model_domain_multi, names(data_list), \(x, y)
  pp_check(x, resp = "FP", type = "intervals_grouped", group = "Domain", ndraws = 1000) +
    ggtitle(y, "FP per image, by domain")
)
```
